Tesla Model Y hunt

All-wheel drive with the HW4 computer, up to 70 000 km and 55 000 €, no damaged cars. Slovakia, Czechia, Austria and Germany.

Good to know

How the total in Slovakia is estimated

Imported cars: about 400 € in Slovak fees (registration 33 € for an electric car, originality check about 100 €, district office approval 100 €, plates about 55 €, recycling fee 30–50 €, document translation about 60 €), plus a typical carrier price to Bratislava. Driving the car home yourself on temporary plates is usually cheaper. No technical inspection is needed for cars under 4 years old.

Slovak cars: only the 33 € ownership transfer.

VAT: a used car bought at the listed gross price owes no further VAT. A car under 6 months old or under 6 000 km counts as a new vehicle for tax, and 23 % Slovak VAT is due on it. In return the foreign VAT should come off the price: a dealer invoices without it, and a private seller can reclaim it from their own tax office after the sale, so ask them to deduct it. For private sales the total shows the worst case, with no deduction. This is not tax advice, so confirm with the tax office before buying one of those.

How HW4 and FSD are judged

FSD was approved in Slovakia on 16 Oct 2026 (in Europe it is called Tesla Assisted Driving). It needs the HW4 computer, also called AI4. Every Juniper has it.

On 2024 cars, Berlin-built Model Ys got HW4 from about September 2024 and Shanghai-built ones from February 2024. Cars first registered in 8–9/2024 fall in the changeover, so they stay "HW4 not confirmed" until the seller shows the screen under Controls › Software. That screen names the computer ("Computer für Full Self-Driving 4" means HW4) and the Autopilot package.

When an ad includes that screen photo, it appears as a small picture in the corner of the car's photo. For the others, ask the seller for it.

Left out and also checked

Photos load from the ad sites. Data is as stated by sellers; check the VIN history before buying.
